Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
825 AM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 821 AM EST Monday...

Have issued a quick update to add isolated flurries/sprinkles to
the forecast this morning. Area webcams indicate some light snow
falling across the northern Greens, and note a few sites in the
Adirondacks are reporting light mist. Any precipitation will be
very light and should remain fairly localized; it will gradually
taper off by early afternoon. No other changes were needed.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 146 AM EST Monday...

1. Dry and warm conditions become established by mid-week.


2. After a period of dry warm weather, chances for showers 
increase towards the end of the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 146 AM EST Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1:  A potent ridge and associated area of surface high 
pressure will become established this week, making it feel as if it 
were still mid-October. In a classic El Nino pattern, deep troughing 
and strong surface lows over the Pacific have caused continuous 
southwest to westerly flow out west, flooding the Great Plains and 
western Canada with warm Pacific air. This has caused temperature 
anomalies in the 20-30+ degree range. This airmass will begin to 
arrive today aloft, but clouds will likely remain stuck under the 
inversion, so it will likely take until Tuesday to warm up. Some 
undercast is likely today due to a shrinking and lowering moisture 
layer. Starting Tuesday, highs in the 50s will prevail though 60 
will be possible in some of the warmest areas. There will be a 
strong, persistent subsidence inversion, and it will aided by the 
fact that significantly more surface heat will be lost at night than 
will be able to be replenished by the sun during the day. 
Radiational cooling will help lows drop into the 20s and 30s, around 
climatological normals.Temperatures at summit level should reach 
well into the 40s and freezing levels look to eclipse 10,000 ft by 
late in the week.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Surface high pressure will be centered south of our 
region Thursday night into Friday, then drift northward across our 
area Saturday before sliding east. This will provide the northern 
New York and Vermont area with mainly dry weather and temperatures 
warmer than seasonal normals. On Sunday a low pressure system north 
of the Great Lakes will track northeastward, and our region will be 
under southerly flow ahead of the cold front. Sunday could be the 
warmest of the period, but will see increasing clouds and chances 
for showers on Sunday as well. We may have a cold front cross the 
area Sunday and bring some scattered rain showers. But there is also 
a possibility with two low pressure centers that the better energy 
associated with each low will pass to our north and to our south, 
leaving us in between without a lot of precipitation. Still much to 
work out before we get to the end of next weekend, but at this time 
this may be our best chance for showers through the period.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 12Z Tuesday...At this time, ceilings range between 
about 0600-2400 ft agl. Over the next few hours, northwest flow 
with adequate moisture will likely keep the region enveloped in 
stratus trapped near to below summit levels of our mountains. 
Ceilings will gradually improve around 16-18z Monday. IFR 
ceilings remain at KSLK but should be lifting in the next couple
hours. Winds will be northwesterly around 5-10 knots, and trend
more westerly beyond that 16-18z time frame. Approaching 00z, 
clouds will begin to gradually scatter, lingering in the 
Northeast Kingdom and Adirondacks longest.

Outlook...
